annotation.title_clean: Responsible Innovation 'Bottom Up'? Using Mobile Robots as a Case
annotation.title_en: Responsible Innovation 'Bottom Up'? Using Mobile Robots as a Case
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Zawieska, K.; Kollakidou, A.; Bodenhagen, L.; Krüger, N.; Martin, C.; Bendt, M. et al.
annotation.venue: Social Robots with AI: Prospects, Risks, and Responsible Methods, Proceedings of Robophilosophy 2024 (IOS Press)
annotation.summary_en: Discussion paper drawing on a Danish case study of mobile robots in retail. It finds values play a limited role in developers' design goals and proposes 'bottom-up' responsible innovation: supervised social experiments and cultural learning among minimally social robots, as an alternative to top-down regulation and standards.
key_provisions_or_claims: Top-down value- and standards-based regulation of social robots is questioned as a starting point.
Developers' design goals for retail mobile robots are ad hoc and give values limited weight.
Proposes responsible innovation bottom-up as supervised social experiment and cultural learning.
Starting with minimally social robots may help citizens avoid anthropomorphic over-interpretation and inappropriate attachment.
Pro and contra views are discussed from the project group's differing perspectives.
